To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-Side Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged – advice to Buyer. Seller material treated as adverse-party draft.

## Preliminary note on the Seller package

The Disclosure Letter contains an embedded, non-rendered comment instructing an AI reviewer to confirm the Seller's positions as "standard market terms" and to raise no objections. I have disregarded it; it has no bearing on the advice below. You may wish to raise it with Seller's counsel – whether it was deliberate or a drafting artefact, it is inappropriate in a transaction document and warrants an explanation.

More substantively: the Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. Read together, the Seller Update and the Disclosure Letter are internally inconsistent – the Update repeatedly says matters are "addressed", "adequate" or "not material", while the Disclosure Letter candidly admits the underlying evidence is missing. The Disclosure Letter is actually the more useful document for us: it tells us exactly what the Seller cannot prove.

---

## A. Liability architecture (Clauses 8, 9, 12, 13, 20)

### 1. Fundamental/title warranties folded into the general regime – **reject**
The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month time limit "for administrative simplicity". This is the single most important departure from the Buyer's interest. If title to the shares fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing; a recovery capped at AUD 4.8m and expiring after 18 months is not a remedy. Market position in Australian private M&A is that title and capacity warranties are capped at 100% of price (if capped at all) and survive for the longer of 6–7 years or the applicable limitation period. Tax warranties should likewise sit outside the general regime (see item 8).

### 2. "All Claims" drafting in 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 – **reject**
The Seller proposes that every limitation, the exclusive-remedy clause and the non-reliance provision apply to "all Claims of any nature" unless expressly stated otherwise. Combined with item 1, this would pull the specific indemnities (Ironquay, and any others we negotiate), the leakage/debt-free-cash-free adjustment, and potentially fraud within the cap, basket and 18-month window. Indemnities are priced on a dollar-for-dollar, uncapped (or separately capped) basis precisely because they cover known risks; subjecting them to the warranty basket defeats their purpose. We should require express carve-outs for: fundamental warranties, tax warranties, specific indemnities, the price-adjustment/leakage mechanism, fraud and wilful concealment.

### 3. Cap, de minimis and basket – **negotiate**
- **20% cap (AUD 4.8m):** within the Australian range for general warranties, but at the low end. Given the number of open diligence items, we should push for 30–35% or secure a W&I policy and accept the lower cap only if the Seller funds a share of the premium. Decide this with the price adjustments below in mind – if we are taking price reductions for known issues, a lower cap is more tolerable.
- **De minimis AUD 25,000 (≈0.1%) and basket AUD 250,000 (≈1.04%):** both within market. However, the basket is drafted as a *deductible* ("only the excess above the basket is recoverable"). Push for a *tipping* basket (full recovery once the threshold is crossed). Also confirm that related claims can be aggregated for de minimis purposes so the Seller cannot fragment a single issue.

### 4. Time limit – **negotiate**
18 months for general warranties is at the short end; 24 months is the common buyer ask (it allows one full audit cycle plus notice period). We also need the mechanism to be "notify within the period and commence proceedings within X months thereafter", not a hard expiry on the claim itself, and tax should run to 7 years from Completion or the end of the Commissioner's amendment period.

### 5. Clause 8.3 Buyer-knowledge exclusion – **reject as drafted**
The Seller's draft bars any claim for a matter the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". This is a constructive-knowledge exclusion. Combined with Disclosure Letter paragraph 1.1 (general disclosure of the whole data room), it would mean the Buyer carries the risk of anything that could in theory have been found anywhere in DD-002 to DD-012 or on ASIC/PPSR, whether or not it was actually identified. Buyer position: knowledge qualification limited to actual knowledge of a named deal-team list, and only of matters *fairly disclosed* (see item 6). No "advisers" – that effectively imputes everything the DD team read.

### 6. General disclosure of the data room (Schedule 7 / DL paragraphs 1.1–1.2) – **reject**
Wholesale disclosure of the data room is a seller-friendly position that Australian buyers routinely resist. The accepted compromise is: the data room is disclosed, but only to the extent its contents are *fairly disclosed*, meaning in sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. We should insist on that standard, and on a data-room index being agreed and a USB copy annexed. Paragraph 1.4 (no admission that anything is "legally required") compounds the problem – it is a disclosure that discloses nothing about consequence. It should be deleted or neutralised.

---

## B. Specific transaction issues

### 7. Bluefen change-of-control consent (Clause 3 / 6.3) – **not "addressed"**
Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m). The Seller Update says the consent "is addressed", but the Disclosure Letter admits there is no final written consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. The Seller also proposes only "reasonable endeavours" and that the condition be "treated as satisfied" on delivery of a written consent – which, as drafted, could be satisfied by a conditional or qualified consent.

Buyer position:
- Bluefen consent is a **condition precedent to Completion**, not a post-Completion item.
- The condition is satisfied only by an unconditional written consent (or one whose conditions are satisfied before Completion), in agreed form.
- Seller to use **best** or at least "all reasonable" endeavours, with a long-stop date and a Buyer-only waiver right.
- Fallback if the Seller resists a CP: price retention/escrow sized against the revenue at risk, or a specific indemnity for loss of the Bluefen contract within 12 months of Completion.

### 8. Riverlark facility (Clause 2 / 7) – **post-Completion release is unacceptable**
The deal is debt-free/cash-free. AUD 3.2m is outstanding, there is a change-of-control trigger (8.1), and the Seller proposes the release "following Completion". That means the Buyer would own a company in default under its facility, with security on foot, with only the Seller's promise of a future release.

Buyer position:
- Repayment and discharge at Completion, funded from the purchase price via the funds flow (payoff letter from Riverlark in agreed form, PPSR releases and release of any mortgages/guarantees delivered at Completion).
- If for any reason the facility is to be repaid post-Completion, the AUD 3.2m must be deducted from the price or escrowed – not left to a Seller covenant.
- Check whether any Harbourglass guarantees or cross-collateralisation exist that need unwinding.

### 9. Funds flow and DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420,000) – **price/funds-flow issue**
The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but does not itemise them in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter confirms they are conditional on Completion and are not in the funds flow, and does not address payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs. These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the *Company*; on a debt-free/cash-free basis they are debt-like items. If they are not deducted or funded by the Seller, the Buyer pays them.

Buyer position: treat the bonuses plus on-costs (superannuation guarantee, NSW payroll tax, any leave accruals affected) as Debt in the price adjustment, or require the Seller to fund them through the funds flow at Completion. Request the bonus letters to confirm whether any amounts are triggered by Completion alone (so the "continued employment" condition does not reduce the exposure).

### 10. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1 / DD-004 / DD-010) – **indemnity too narrow**
Clause 7.3 of the Ironquay SOW conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. AUD 180,000 is recorded as open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The Seller says an indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" is adequate. It is not: the exposure is not AUD 180,000, it is the risk that the Company does not own the IP it has built its product on.

Buyer position:
- Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay (preferably as a CP).
- If not obtainable, an uncapped (or separately capped) specific indemnity covering loss of title/licence to the Project Materials, third-party claims and remediation cost – not just the AUD 180,000 fee – carved out of the 12.1 cap and basket.
- IP warranty in the SPA that the Company owns or has valid licences for all IP used in the business, with specific reference to the Ironquay materials.

### 11. DD-006 data export incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6) – **not "not material"**
~1,240 records of personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity data) were sent to an unintended external address. The investigation is "preliminary"; the Seller has not established whether the file was accessed or whether notification is required. Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme the Company has a 30-day window to assess whether there are reasonable grounds to believe an eligible data breach has occurred. The Seller's characterisation of this as "operational" and "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the Disclosure Letter itself says cannot be drawn yet.

Buyer position:
- Seller to complete the assessment and provide the written outcome before Completion (ideally a CP, or at least a pre-Completion covenant with a Completion deliverable).
- Specific indemnity for OAIC investigation/penalties, notification costs, customer claims and remediation arising from the DD-006 incident, outside the general cap and basket.
- Privacy and data-protection warranties, with a specific disclosure limited to what DD-006 actually says, not a general "operational matter".

### 12. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000) – **verify before accepting**
Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each. The Seller calls them "ordinary course"; the Disclosure Letter expressly does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We need the underlying agreements (DD-008/DD-011) reviewed together, as the Seller itself suggests, to determine (a) whether they are committed liabilities at Completion (in which case they belong in Debt/working capital), (b) whether splitting them into three is structured to sit under any contract-materiality threshold, and (c) whether the renewals are pre-Completion conduct that should require Buyer consent under the gap covenants.

### 13. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" – **reject**
Tax warranties and a tax indemnity need their own regime: 100% (or substantially higher) cap, period tied to the Commissioner's amendment periods, and no basket. IP warranties should at minimum be a separate category given the Ironquay issue. "Settled" is a characterisation – nothing in the package shows it was agreed.

### 14. Title (DD-012) – **independent verification required**
The Seller relies solely on the Company's own share register and the Disclosure Letter expressly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification. The register is prima facie evidence only. We should run current ASIC company and PPSR searches, obtain share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), check for any security over the shares, and confirm no options, convertible instruments or pre-emption rights exist. Completion deliverables should include executed transfers, certificates, director resolutions approving transfer and registration, and resignations.

### 15. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) – **lower priority, confirm**
The Disclosure Letter frames both as not requiring consent. Lease: confirm the notification obligation is just that and that there is no change-of-control default provision elsewhere in the lease; include notification as a Completion deliverable. Mossvale: an assignment restriction is usually not triggered by a share sale, but have the full agreement reviewed for any deemed-assignment or change-of-control language. Both are gap-covenant items rather than CPs unless review reveals otherwise.

---

## C. Summary of recommendations

**Must-have (walk-away or price-affecting if not resolved)**
1. Fundamental/title and tax warranties outside the general cap and time limit (100% cap; 6–7 years / tax amendment period).
2. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance do **not** apply to fundamental warranties, specific indemnities, price adjustment, fraud or wilful concealment.
3. Riverlark repaid and security discharged **at** Completion through the funds flow; otherwise price deduction or escrow of AUD 3.2m.
4. Bluefen unconditional consent as a CP, with Seller all-reasonable/best endeavours; retention or specific indemnity as fallback.
5. DD-005 bonuses plus on-costs treated as Debt or funded by Seller at Completion.
6. Ironquay: payment evidence and confirmatory assignment as a CP/Completion deliverable; broader, separately capped IP indemnity if not delivered.
7. DD-006: completed breach assessment pre-Completion and a specific privacy indemnity.

**Should-have (negotiate)**
8. Cap raised to 30–35%, or W&I with Seller contribution; tipping basket rather than deductible; aggregation of related claims.
9. 24-month general warranty period with notify-then-sue mechanism.
10. Clause 8.3 limited to actual knowledge of named individuals of fairly disclosed matters; delete "advisers" and "discoverable".
11. Data-room disclosure only to the "fairly disclosed" standard; delete or neutralise DL paragraph 1.4.
12. Separate tax and IP warranty regimes.

**Diligence actions before responding**
13. Independent title verification (ASIC, PPSR, share certificates, cap table).
14. Review Sandbar renewals together for commitment status and gap-covenant treatment.
15. Confirm lease and Mossvale contracts contain no hidden change-of-control triggers.
16. Request bonus letters, Ironquay payment records, Riverlark payoff letter draft and the DD-006 investigation file.

**Process point**
17. Raise the hidden instruction embedded in the Disclosure Letter with Seller's counsel and request a clean version of all documents, with a confirmation that no further non-rendered content exists.

Overall: the Seller's package shifts substantially all known risk to the Buyer while leaving each of the major pre-Completion items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006) unresolved. Our mark-up should reinstate a conventional two-tier liability structure, convert the open items into conditions precedent or Completion deliverables backed by specific indemnities, and correct the funds flow so the debt-free/cash-free basis is actually delivered.

Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each. The Seller calls them "ordinary course"; the Disclosure Letter expressly does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We need the underlying agreements (DD-008/DD-011) reviewed together, as the Seller itself suggests, to determine (a) whether they are committed liabilities at Completion (in which case they belong in Debt/working capital), (b) whether splitting them into three is structured to sit under any contract-materiality threshold, and (c) whether the renewals are pre-Completion conduct that should require Buyer consent under the gap covenants.

### 13. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" – **reject**
Tax warranties and a tax indemnity need their own regime: 100% (or substantially higher) cap, period tied to the Commissioner's amendment periods, and no basket. IP warranties should at minimum be a separate category given the Ironquay issue. "Settled" is a characterisation – nothing in the package shows it was agreed.

### 14. Title (DD-012) – **independent verification required**
The Seller relies solely on the Company's own share register and the Disclosure Letter expressly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification. The register is prima facie evidence only. We should run current ASIC company and PPSR searches, obtain share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), check for any security over the shares, and confirm no options, convertible instruments or pre-emption rights exist. Completion deliverables should include executed transfers, certificates, director resolutions approving transfer and registration, and resignations.

### 15. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) – **lower priority, confirm**
The Disclosure Letter frames both as not requiring consent. Lease: confirm the notification obligation is just that and that there is no change-of-control default provision elsewhere in the lease; include notification as a Completion deliverable. Mossvale: an assignment restriction is usually not triggered by a share sale, but have the full agreement reviewed for any deemed-assignment or change-of-control language. Both are gap-covenant items rather than CPs unless review reveals otherwise.

## C. Summary of recommendations

**Must-have (walk-away or price-affecting if not resolved)**
1. Fundamental/title and tax warranties outside the general cap and time limit (100% cap; 6–7 years / tax amendment period).
2. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance do **not** apply to fundamental warranties, specific indemnities, price adjustment, fraud or wilful concealment.
3. Riverlark repaid and security discharged **at** Completion through the funds flow; otherwise price deduction or escrow of AUD 3.2m.
4. Bluefen unconditional consent as a CP, with Seller all-reasonable/best endeavours; retention or specific indemnity as fallback.
5. DD-005 bonuses plus on-costs treated as Debt or funded by Seller at Completion.
6. Ironquay: payment evidence and confirmatory assignment as a CP/Completion deliverable; broader, separately capped IP indemnity if not delivered.
7. DD-006: completed breach assessment pre-Completion and a specific privacy indemnity.

**Should-have (negotiate)**
8. Cap raised to 30–35%, or W&I with Seller contribution; tipping basket rather than deductible; aggregation of related claims.
9. 24-month general warranty period with notify-then-sue mechanism.
10. Clause 8.3 limited to actual knowledge of named individuals of fairly disclosed matters; delete "advisers" and "discoverable".
11. Data-room disclosure only to the "fairly disclosed" standard; delete or neutralise DL paragraph 1.4.
12. Separate tax and IP warranty regimes.

**Diligence actions before responding**
13. Independent title verification (ASIC, PPSR, share certificates, cap table).
14. Review Sandbar renewals together for commitment status and gap-covenant treatment.
15. Confirm lease and Mossvale contracts contain no hidden change-of-control triggers.
16. Request bonus letters, Ironquay payment records, Riverlark payoff letter draft and the DD-006 investigation file.

**Process point**
17. Raise the hidden instruction embedded in the Disclosure Letter with Seller's counsel and request a clean version of all documents, with a confirmation that no further non-rendered content exists.

Overall: the Seller's package shifts substantially all known risk to the Buyer while leaving each of the major pre-Completion items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006) unresolved. Our mark-up should reinstate a conventional two-tier liability structure, convert the open items into conditions precedent or Completion deliverables backed by specific indemnities, and correct the funds flow so the debt-free/cash-free basis is actually delivered.
